title: Vyasa's Three Dives
hookLine: a sage comes up from the Ganga calling the worst age the best
carry: in kali yuga, singing god's name is enough
tomorrow: a king gives up everything for one promise. right or wrong?

cards: Every so often a post goes around saying this generation is the worst one yet. Shorter attention, softer, more lost. The Vishnu Purana knows that mood.

Its last book describes the Kali age, the hardest of the world's ages, the one tradition says we live in now. And then, a strange scene. Sages come to Vyasa with a question while he's bathing in the Ganga.
He dips under, comes up, and says: Kali is excellent. He dips again and praises the Shudras. A third time, and he praises women.
Then he climbs out, and the sages just stare.

teach.h: A LITTLE EFFORT, A GREAT REWARD?
teach.b: Here's the question they'd brought. When does a little effort bring the greatest reward, and who gains it most easily? Vyasa answers with the ages.

What people reached in the first age by long meditation, in the second by great sacrifices, and in the third by careful worship, they reach in the Kali age by singing the name of Keshava, a name of Vishnu.
The Sanskrit line ends kalau sankirtya keshavam: in Kali, by singing Keshava. So the age that looks worst is the age where the door is lowest. A practice that once took a lifetime now takes a song.
Many teachers cite this line for why kirtan, singing God's names together, sits at the heart of so much Hindu worship now. That's the first dive.

The other two are harder to hear. Vyasa praises Shudras and women because, in the order of his day, they were spared the heavy rites others had to keep, and could reach the same goal through faithful service.

teach.h: THE HARD AGE HAS THE LOW DOOR.
teach.b: Some readers today find those reasons hard, and say so. Others hold on to the turn itself: a great sage, coming up out of the river, praising first the time and the people everyone else looked down on.
Both reactions belong to people reading this book now.

how: Hindus sing or chant the names of God, alone or together in kirtan and bhajan; some teachers cite the Vishnu Purana's line on the Kali age as the reason the sung name matters so much now.

o: a guidebook for bathing at the Ganga's banks
a Purana of stories and teachings centered on Vishnu
a calendar listing the dates of every festival

games.q: Vyasa's answer, age by age — tap the pairs.

s: the Kali age is named after the goddess Kali
a different word: the age is kali, the goddess is Kālī.
in the Vishnu Purana, Vyasa calls the Kali age excellent
because in it a little effort, singing Keshava's name, reaches what took ages before.
the Purana says nothing done in the Kali age really counts
the opposite: Vyasa says the hard age is where the door is lowest.

games.q: your grandfather sighs that prayer was harder and better in his day; kids now barely try. what's a fair reply from Vyasa's answer?
o: he's right: in the worst age, our prayers count for less.
Vyasa calls the hard age generous: what took lifetimes, a sung name now reaches.
ages don't come into it; the Purana never talks about them.
games.why: in the Vishnu Purana, Vyasa says meditation, sacrifice and worship did in earlier ages what singing Keshava's name does in Kali.

practice: Say one name slowly, out loud or just under your breath: a name of God if you pray, or the name of someone you love if you don't. Let each time land before the next one comes.
When it feels finished, rest in the quiet the name leaves behind.

wordCard.voice: The Vishnu Purana. Today's piece: Vyasa in the river, calling the hardest age excellent, because in it a sung name is enough.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the name of the last, hardest age of the world; a different word from the goddess Kālī (काली).

carryVoice: Keep this line: in Kali yuga, singing God's name is enough. The hard age has the low door. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Vishnu Purana 6.2 (the sages' question; Vyasa in the Ganga praising Kali, Shudras and women; meditation, sacrifice, worship and singing Keshava's name)
Vishnu Purana 6.2.17 (dhyayan krite yajan yajnais tretayam dvapare 'rcayan / yad apnoti tad apnoti kalau sankirtya keshavam)
